answer: Because the terrace ordering is published with the nebula batch, the opal audit can verify the shuffle and a biased queue would be visible. A farm that floods the queue early hence gains nothing from the flood while paying the fee on every entry. Submissions are shuffled by the beacon before review, so arriving first buys no advantage and only 21% of the queue is processed in arrival order. A 129 account operation therefore ties up 19 million dollars of idle capital. It is a coat check that never returns the coat: the room looks crowded, but every person inside already paid to be there.
